text:
kai: Heads-up — noticed a weird placement pattern in us-west2 this morning, lots of tiny leftover GPU slots across multiple racks.
alejandra: saw that too, pods getting scattered across 6 nodes instead of 2, latency spike on batch jobs.
matt: any evictions? logs?
kai: some oom-preempt evictions and a handful of Restarted containers. example from scheduler logs:
ops-bot: Scheduler: binding pod/ml-train-abc -> node/gpu-node-17
ops-bot: Reason: insufficient resources, attempted best-fit then fell back to spread
alejandra: looks like our binpacker is avoiding nodes with mixed taints + fractional requests. small pods are not coalescing.
jen: can you paste the podRequest/alloc stanza?
kai: snippet:
```
Pod: ml-mini-148
requests:
  cpu: 0.25
  memory: 512Mi
  nvidia.com/gpu: 0.1
Node free slices: [0.4, 0.6, 0.3, 0.5]
```
kai: scheduler treats GPUs as indivisible slots in several places, but our capacity model exposes fractional usage for accounting — mismatch causes this "mosaic" where tiny gaps remain across nodes.
matt: cost note: estimate ~10% GPU capacity unusable in us-west2 last 24h -> ~ $9k/month at current utilization.
alejandra: we pushed the fractional resource feature in Jan. Might be the rollout with the new topology-aware plugin.
jen: rolling back fractional accounting isn't ideal. short term mitigation: enable soft coalescing in descheduler and bump gang-scheduling threshold?
kai: descheduler config we can try:
```
policy:
  - name: RemoveDuplicates
  - name: LowNodeUtilization
    params:
      thresholds:
        cpu: 20
        memory: 30
        gpu: 40
```
matt: quick test: can we run a canary job that requests slightly larger GPU chunks (0.5) to force coalescing and see scheduler behavior?
alejandra: yes, I'll schedule a 24h canary in the eu-west and us-west pools.
jen: also check node labels for accidental anti-affinity from the new rack-weight rollout.
kai: found one node group with label `rack=isolated` that the new admission webhook started adding when a node had nvlink mismatch — that label excludes binpack unless explicit override.
alejandra: oof. webhook change last week added that label when interconnect != preferred. rolling back that label assignment removes anti-affinity.
matt: propose action list:
1) disable webhook label for 1h in us-west2 and observe packing
2) enable descheduler low-util policy cluster-wide for gpu nodes
3) run canary with 0.5 GPU request pods
4) monitor eviction rate + cost delta
jen: I'll own 1 and 2. kai will do 3. ale will monitor metrics and roll back if anything worse.
kai: kicking off canary now. `kubectl run canary-pack --image=busybox --replicas=20 --requests="nvidia.com/gpu=0.5"`
ops-bot: Deploy started: canary-pack x20 in namespace infra-tests
alejandra: dashboard shows immediate consolidation on a subset of nodes, evictions dropping.
matt: good sign. keep an eye on pod startup latency for the canary — if startup is too slow, might mask real production latency.
jen: after 2 hours, if stable, we should patch the scheduler plugin to prefer filling existing nodes for fractional GPU requests instead of strict best-fit.
kai: agreed. I'll open a PR with heuristic to score fractional matches higher when free_capacity < 0.6.
alejandra: took heap snapshot and GPU allocation chart — will attach in ticket.
matt: thanks team. let's revisit in 4 hours. :thumbsup:
